title: Complicated molecules generally do not reach minimum-energy configurations

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Complicated molecules generally do not reach minimum-energy configurations

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Although simple molecules may settle into minimum-energy configurations, complicated molecules typically do not; they explore configurations by an explicit evolution process, so nature does not actually solve hard constraint-satisfaction problems as traditional models idealize.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: while in simple cases complicated molecules may for example arrange themselves in configurations that minimize energy, the evidence is that in more complicated cases they typically do not.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “The Validity of the Principle” (from p. 726), p. 729. Scope: molecular configurations such as large biomolecules and glasses

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.61

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Many observed molecular structures and energy models exist, enabling tests in selected domains. Coverage and reliable global-minimum identification are insufficient for the broad statement about complicated molecules generally.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For preregistered classes of large molecules and glasses, compare experimentally observed structures with independently calculated global minimum-energy structures and characterized metastable basins. A predominance of demonstrably metastable observed states supports the restricted claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Observed structures depend on solvent, temperature, kinetics, and measurement conditions.

Global energy minima are computationally difficult to establish.

Public structures are biased toward tractable molecules and do not cover glasses broadly.

fields.value:
data existence: 0.75
data adequacy: 0.45

discriminating power: 0.6
analysis feasibility: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public structure databases cover many small molecules and many proteins, which is enough to test a size-restricted version of the contrast. Glasses and the full range of complicated molecules are not in one open energy catalog, and the comparison depends on the energy function. The analysis is a multi-month harmonization, not a standard short computation, and it would still leave the word typically tied to the chosen sample.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For a size cutoff separating simple and complicated molecules, compare experimental structures with the global minimum of a stated energy function. The claim is supported if complicated cases are typically trapped above that minimum while simple cases sit at it, and refuted if complicated molecules are typically found at the global minimum.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Minimum energy can mean potential energy, free energy, or a glass basin, and these disagree.

Force fields can mis-rank minima, so an apparent miss may be an error in the energy model.
